This is a concrete, test-backed specification. The `valid-annotation-format` rule has been extended to support configurable story and requirement patterns via both nested (`story.pattern` / `req.pattern`) and flat (`storyPathPattern` / `requirementIdPattern`) options, with corresponding example fields for error messages. Invalid regex configurations are detected at rule-option-resolution time, produce clear `invalidRuleConfiguration` diagnostics, and safely fall back to default patterns, preserving previous behaviour.
JSON Schema for the rule options includes all new fields and disallows unknown properties, aligning with ESLint configuration best practices. Error messages dynamically incorporate configured example strings, with precedence rules between nested and flat forms verified by tests. The rule’s default patterns remain aligned with `valid-story-reference`’s default `storyDirectories` (`docs/stories`) so format validation and path/existence validation interoperate cleanly.
Extensive unit tests in `tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts` are explicitly tagged with Story 010.1 and its requirement IDs, and they cover: custom patterns (nested and flat), custom example messages, invalid pattern handling with fallback, and precedence between nested and flat configuration. All such tests pass in the recorded jest run. Based on this evidence, all acceptance criteria and story-level requirements for 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS are satisfied.
